items.summary_auto: The U.S. Federal Aviation Administration has paused installing routers linked to last week's ground stop that caused chaos for travellers, the agency said Tuesday.

items.title: Grand Theft Auto VI nominated for game of the year, even though it isn't out yet
items.summary_auto: Grand Theft Auto VI has yet to be released to the general public, but already it's being touted as the potential game of the year. The Game Awards released its nomination list on Tuesday, with Grand Theft Auto VI receiving eight nominations.

items.title: 'Crypto King' or 'Lying King'? Aiden Pleterski says he was neither at alleged kidnappers' trial
items.summary_auto: Aiden Pleterski denied ever calling himself the "Crypto King" — or paying for a Forbes sponsored article that did — under cross-examination at the trial for his alleged kidnappers in Toronto on Tuesday.

items.summary_auto: Police say injuries are not life-threatening and cleanup is underway.

items.title: Canada's national emergency alert system will sound off Wednesday for testing
items.summary_auto: Canada's National Public Alerting System is running tests of its Alert Ready system Wednesday across all provinces and territories. Alert Ready delivers alerts about critical events such as tornadoes, flooding, fires and Amber alerts.

items.title: Calgary high school says too many students are getting food delivered
items.summary_auto: A Calgary high school sent parents a memo this week asking them to rein in their children’s increasing use of food delivery apps like Uber Eats and DoorDash during school hours.

items.title: U.K. sanctions Israeli companies involved in building illegal settlements in West Bank
items.summary_auto: Britain said on Tuesday it would impose sanctions on eight Israeli construction companies involved in building settlements in the occupied West Bank, as part of its effort to protect the idea of a two-state solution.

items.title: Meet the 2027 Grammy best new artist nominees
items.summary_auto: The 2027 Grammy nominees for best new artist dropped Monday, putting a spotlight on who's reshaping the music scene. If you want to keep your playlist fresh — or at least know what everyone in the group chat is talking about — here are the names shaping the conversation.

items.title: Canada has extended and expanded its deal with China. Here's how it affects different sectors
items.summary_auto: Prime Minister Mark Carney and Chinese President Xi Jinping agreed to deepen economic and trade ties at a bilateral meeting in Shenzhen, China, on Tuesday, expanding a tariff deal to include relief on Canadian exports worth roughly $400 million, including some pork and seafood products. Here's a breakdown.

items.title: Convicted rapist Russell Brand under investigation for claiming innocence from behind bars
items.summary_auto: The Ministry of Justice in the U.K. is investigating whether comedian and convicted rapist Russell Brand is guilty of breaking prison rules after his wife shared a message from Brand on his YouTube channel claiming his innocence.

items.title: New middle-class tax cut coming next year, Manitoba government says in throne speech
items.summary_auto: Manitoba's NDP government is promising a "broad middle-class tax cut," free shingles vaccinations for seniors and a new crime unit targeting fraud and corruption.

items.title: Who pays when climate disasters strike?
items.summary_auto: Nepal has become the first country to have funding provisionally set aside from the UN's Fund for Responding to Loss and Damage following devastating flooding. But Nepal needs billions to rebuild, and the fund has set aside just millions. From the Himalayas to the COP31 climate summit, can the international community deliver the help vulnerable countries need?

items.title: Hamilton police investigate after witnesses report group shouting pro-Nazi comments at demonstration
items.summary_auto: Hamilton police are investigating after receiving reports that a group of about 20 to 25 people dressed in black and wearing masks were shouting pro-Nazi comments at a downtown demonstration Saturday.

items.title: Ukraine cripples Crimean bridge in blow to Putin before meeting with Xi, Trump
items.summary_auto: Ukrainian drones and missiles destroyed the central road section of the bridge linking Russia and Crimea on Tuesday, inflicting a military and symbolic blow on Russian President Vladimir Putin two days before he is due to meet the leaders of China and the U.S.

items.title: WNBA commissioner search underway with Cathy Engelbert to retire at year's end
items.summary_auto: The search for a successor to WNBA commissioner Cathy Engelbert is well underway with more than a dozen candidates in the mix so far.

items.title: How China is positioning itself as a global leader as it hosts Trump, Putin
items.summary_auto: As China welcomes world leaders to the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation forum this week in Shenzhen, it presents a very different nation than the one that last hosted the event in 2014.

items.title: Russian figure skaters out of Grand Prix event due to Finland's ban on Russian athletes
items.summary_auto: Seven Russian figure skaters have been withdrawn from a Grand Prix event in Finland this week after the Finnish government barred Russian athletes from entering the country, the Russian Figure Skating Federation said Tuesday.

items.title: The U.S. has officially lost its measles elimination status amid worst outbreak in 35 years
items.summary_auto: After a deadly year for measles outbreaks, the U.S. has officially lost its measles elimination status, more than a quarter of a century after it first achieved the distinction. The news comes after Canada lost its measles elimination status last November, a distinction it had held for 28 years.

items.title: Ontario secondary school teachers vote 96% in favour of strike mandate

items.title: TC Energy plans Alberta pipeline expansion to serve natural gas demand
items.summary_auto: TC Energy Corp. is looking to seize on booming natural gas demand in Alberta, announcing plans Monday to expand its pipeline network to add an initial billion cubic feet per day of new capacity.

items.summary_auto: Krampus, a European Christmas folk creature, has been banned from Strathory, Ont. 's Santa Claus parade despite winning second place in the event's costume contest last year. Organizers say there were complaints that the figure wasn't family friendly.

items.title: South Korea to check student collars, eyeglasses at university entrance exams after cheating admission
items.summary_auto: South Korea will tighten checks on students taking the high-stakes national university entrance exam this week, Prime Minister Han Seong-sook said, after a candidate in another test confessed to using a hidden ​camera and AI to cheat.

items.summary_auto: Telus says it's decided not to proceed with co-developing two Vancouver data centres, and will instead turn its focus to expanding an existing data centre in Kamloops, B.C.

items.title: Former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang signals willingness to return as CEO
items.summary_auto: The former CEO of the top AI chipmaker who resigned last week amid a spying scandal said he "would be honoured" ‌to come back as CEO if the board decided his return would be in the best interest of shareholders and employees. Jensen Huang's first public statement since he resigned last week comes as the former leader agreed to answer questions from U.S. lawmakers next month, and as Nvidia's board formed a committee to address export and security concerns.

items.title: Drivers line up as fuel price briefly falls below $1 in northwest Winnipeg
items.summary_auto: Drivers lined up Tuesday morning at one Winnipeg gas station where gas prices fell below the $1 mark. The price at the McPhillips Street Domo had climbed to 113.9 by the afternoon.

items.title: Investigate Trump or work with him? Democrats debate best path forward
items.summary_auto: Still giddy from their sweeping midterm victory, the Democrats now face a dilemma over what to do next. Some factions within the party are urging a strong push to investigate U.S. President Donald Trump, his family and his allies over allegations of corruption. Others insist the Democrats must stay laser-focused on the cost of living.
